claim:
For \(\frac12<\beta<1\), let
\[
N_\beta(u,v)=\max\{|u|,|v|,\beta(|u|+|v|)\},
\qquad
X_\beta=(\mathbb R^2,N_\beta),
\]
and put \(c_\beta=(1-\beta)/\beta\). The known modified von Neumann--Jordan constant
\[
C'_{\mathrm{NJ}}(X_\beta)
=
\sup_{x,y\in S_{X_\beta}}
\frac{N_\beta(x+y)^2+N_\beta(x-y)^2}{4}
\]
has the following complete equality classification. If \(\frac12<\beta<1/\sqrt2\), equality holds exactly when, up to a common signed-coordinate permutation, exchange of \(x,y\), and changing the sign of either vector,
\[
(x,y)=((1,c_\beta),(1,-c_\beta)).
\]
If \(1/\sqrt2<\beta<1\), equality holds exactly when, under the same equivalences,
\[
(x,y)=((1,c_\beta),(c_\beta,1)).
\]
At \(\beta=1/\sqrt2\), the equality set is the union of these two coordinate classes. Thus the classical value formula undergoes a genuine extremizer-geometry transition at the regular-octagon parameter: below it the extremal chords are coordinate-axis directions, above it they are diagonal directions, and at the transition both occur.
integrity: The value formulas are prior results. The new content is the complete equality-pair classification obtained by tracking equality in sharp Euclidean comparisons and the parallelogram identity. The vertex step is exhaustive only after the proof forces both variables to the eight vertices.
scientific_limitations: The equality classification is for the real octagonal family with one-half < beta < 1; the square and diamond endpoints are excluded because their equality sets degenerate. No classification is claimed for arbitrary absolute normalized norms.
title: Rigidity and phase transition of modified von Neumann--Jordan extremizers in a classical octagonal family
